A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gumbel Reranking work. Their main text and Appendices A-G, including equations, algorithms, figures and tables, are readable and support a full comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and generation experiments in Tables 1-4, Gumbel-noise and learnable-weight analyses in Sections 4.4-4.5, and hyperparameter experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark tables, ablations and appendix sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same differentiable masked attention, Gumbel sampling, relaxed top-k aggregation and language-loss optimization. The learnable document-weight procedure in Algorithm 2 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate HotpotQA, 2WikiHop, MuSiQue, NQ and TQA. The single-hop and multi-hop coverage, mining/reranking/generation settings, and indirect-evidence scenario are unchanged.

E2.justification: EMDR, PDist, LOOP and ADist remain the evaluated training baselines in corresponding comparisons in Tables 1-4. Figure 5 also retains the same perplexity, leave-one-out perplexity and attention-score comparators.

E3.justification: Reader and reranker configurations, fixed-reader training, evaluation metrics and candidate construction match. Both retain DPR retrieval of 20 documents for NQ/TQA, the same multi-hop distractor settings, and Appendix E's filtering rule and sample counts.

E4.justification: The Gumbel-noise ablation, analysis without reranker text priors, and temperature/scaling sensitivity studies are retained without changes to their questions or evidence (Sections 4.4-4.5 and Appendices A and F).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The point-estimate tables and training-curve reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 and Figures 4-7 retain the same results and trends. For example, Table 2 reports FiD-Large reranker-setting recall of 72.2 for G-Rerank and 61.8 for EMDR in both versions. The NQ Gumbel ablation also remains 46.2 versus 12.7 EM.

T1.justification: Equations 1-7, the document-independence requirements, and the mathematical formulations in Appendices B, D and F are unchanged. No definitions, derivations or proofs are added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about end-to-end reranker optimization, reducing the training-inference gap and capturing document interdependencies. The headline 10.4% HotpotQA recall-improvement claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of subset sampling and the Gumbel ablation remain the same. Section 6 retains the parallel pre-filling and hyperparameter limitations, while Appendix E retains the qualification about ambiguous direct versus indirect evidence.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page code-availability footnote with a hyperlink to the Gumbel-Reranking repository; v1 has no corresponding code-access pointer. Other technical documentation and Appendix G's dataset access and license information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2, Appendices B-D and the bibliography are unchanged. No prior work is added or removed, and the novelty framing is retained.

P1.justification: v2 expands and corrects affiliations, adds internship/correspondence/code footnotes and a funding acknowledgement, and makes small capitalization and wording edits. The scientific exposition and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page author and footnote layout changes, text reflows across columns and pages, and page-number footers disappear. The conclusion moves from PDF page 8 to page 9. Figures 1-8 and Tables 1-5 retain their content, captions and display structures.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer and explicit funding and internship disclosures, improving code discoverability and research transparency. These are limited documentation gains: the scientific argument and evidence are unchanged, and repository completeness or usability cannot be established from the PDFs.
